Article Title: Supreme Court relaxes order mandating Coalgate appeals only before itself, allows Delhi high court to hear them
Article Text:
Apex court on Coalgate case

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Diluting its 12year-old order mandating appeals to be filed only in the Supreme Court against trial court orders in coal block allotment scam cases, the SC Wednesday said the prosecution and accused can move the Delhi HC challenging acquittals or convictions recorded by the special judge.Taking up the long pending appeals in coal scam cases, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “Why did the Supreme Court invite such a burden on itself ? There may have been certain concerns at some point of time. But can the Supreme Court denude the high court’s constitutionally conferred powers to hear appeals against trial court orders? Powers of the high court to hear appeals against trial court is part of the basic structure. ”Appearing for some of the accused in coal scam cases, senior advocate Kapil Sibal said SC should not be the first forum of appeal against trial court orders. However, SC-appointed special public prosecutor R S Cheema said trials in two-thirds of the cases have been over and that the restraint on approaching the high court against interim orders of the special judge should continue.The bench agreed with Cheema but said that in those cases where the trial court has recorded either conviction or acquittal, the appeal by person or prosecution must challenge it before the Delhi high court.In Sept 2014, Supreme Court had cancelled 204 of the 218 coal block allocations and directed that all appeals against framing of charge, quashing of case and bail petitions must be filed only before the Supreme Court and not Delhi high court.This restriction was imposed to prevent accused from delaying trials.Sibal, who was a minister in the Congress-headed UPA govt when the coal scam and 2G scam cases rocked its electoral support base, told the court that the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) had made an omnibus calculation about alleged loss to exchequer because of the coal block allocations, without quantifying loss attributable to individual coal blocks.“We have challenged the basis on which such calculations were made by the CAG. Moreover, we have also questioned whether mere allotment of coal blocks would amount to corrupt practice without any mining having taken place at all,” Sibal said.The top court asked Cheema and the counsel for accused to help in categorizing the bunch of cases for hearing from Aug 18.
Article Summary: The supreme court said the prosecution and accused can move the delhi hc challenging acquittals or convictions recorded by the special judge. In sept 2014, supreme court had cancelled 204 of the 218 coal block allocations and directed that all appeals against framing of charge, quashing of case and bail petitions must be filed only before the supreme court.

Article Title: Over 1 lakh schools in India functioning with a single teacher
Article Text:
File photo

The single-teacher-school data indicates that favourable national averages continue to conceal sharp local imbalances in teacher availability

‘Vacancies due to retirement, resignations, enrolment change’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: More than one lakh schools — government, government-aided and private — are functioning with a single teacher, with Andhra Pradesh alone accounting for over 16,000, government data has revealed, highlighting severe deployment gaps despite the country’s overall pupil-teacher ratio remaining within national norms.The education ministry cited national pupil-teacher ratios of 19 at primary level, 17 at upper primary, 15 at secondary and 23 at higher secondary — all within the limits envisaged under National Education Policy. However, the single-teacher-school data indicates that favourable national averages continue to conceal sharp local imbalances in teacher availability.According to UDISE+ data for 2025-26, India has 1,00,843 single-teacher schools across all management categories. Andhra Pradesh tops the list with 16,357 such schools — more than 16% of the national total — followed by Jharkhand (9,827) and Maharashtra (9,269). Karnataka has 8,042 single-teacher schools, UP 7,874, Rajasthan 7,200 and West Bengal 6,769. Together, these seven states account for nearly 65% of all schools operating with one teacher.The problem is spread across regions rather than being confined to poorer or geographically difficult states.Telangana has 4,793 such schools, Tamil Nadu 3,957 and Assam 3,159. Himachal Pradesh has 3,128, Uttarakhand 2,655 and Chhattisgarh 2,461. At the other end, Kerala reported 67 singleteacher schools, Nagaland 35, Sikkim 31, Ladakh 28, Delhi seven and Andaman and Nicobar Islands one.The figures were provided by MoS for education Jayant Chaudhary in response to a RS question on teacher vacancies. While the question sought data specifically for government schools, the annexure on single-teacher institutions covers schools under all managements.The ministry did not provide state-wise sanctioned posts or vacancies, saying recruitment, service conditions and deployment of teachers were handled by state governments and UT administrations. It attributed vacancies to retirement, resignation, creation of posts, staff rationalisation and changing enrolment, including in rural, tribal and aspirational districts.Government said states were regularly advised to fill posts through transparent, merit-based recruitment and use technology for forecasting teacher requirements. Financial support was also provided under Samagra Shiksha to maintain prescribed pupil-teacher ratios.
Article Summary: Andhra pradesh tops the list with 16,357 such schools. Karnataka has 8,042 single-teacher schools, up 7,874, rajasthan 7,200 and west bengal 6,769. Telangana has 4,793 such schools, tamil nadu 3,957 and assam 3,159.

Article Title: Supreme Court bars government from post facto green clearance to projects
Article Text:
File photo

Supreme Court: Follow 2006 notification for prior EC nod

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Wednesday saved central and state projects worth Rs 20,000 crore from demolition for want of prior environmental clearance but permanently prohibited govt from granting post facto EC and quashed Centre’s 2021 Office Memorandum for keeping a window indefinitely open for projects to seek such green nods.Rescinding a part of its earlier decision that had quashed Centre’s 2017 notification, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M Pancholi said the 2017 notification was valid as it had a limited period window for clearance to projects of significant public interest.However, the bench concurred with the earlier decision to quash the 2021 OM as finding it to be an open-ended administrative order was tantamount to a perpetual amnesty regime for grant of EC to projects undertaken without prior green nod. It said the OM was without having any rational nexus with public interest, and hence is in breach of Environment Protection Act, 1986.Supreme Court said its judgment will operate prospectively, and the ECs granted to various projects under the 2017 notification and the 2021 OM would remain valid. “The prior EC regime under the 2006 notification is mandatory and unless amended by an appropriate notification, would not accommodate grant of post facto EC or retention of projects where constructions have commenced or processes begun without a valid EC,” it said.Supreme Court directed scrupulous adherence to the 2006 notification mandating prior EC clearance for projects. The bench said, “Govt is restrained from issuing administrative orders in future for grant of EC in respect of projects which have commenced in contravention of the prior EC regime under the 2006 notification.”Pending applications (for grant of post facto EC) shall be dealt with in accordance with the law, it said, adding that “no fresh application for grant of EC under the aforesaid instruments (2014 notification or 2021 OM) shall be entertained.”Writing the judgment, Justice Bagchi said the court aimed to strike a balance between an “existential right of all living beings both present and future to a pollution-free environment and an aspirational right to development of a sixth of the world’s population”.The bench, however, noted that Centre has powers under Jan Vishwas Act to decriminalise violations of EP Act by notifying amnesty schemes with regard to such classes or categories of non-compliant projects whose sustainability is necessary to subserve larger public interest.In Nov last year, a bench of then CJI B R Gavai and Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and K Vinod Chandran by two to one majority decided to review the court’s May 2025 decision by Justices A S Oka and Bhuyan which had quashed all post facto green clearance which left public projects worth Rs 20,000 crore vulnerable to demolition.
Article Summary: Supreme court quashes centre’s 2021 office memorandum for keeping a window indefinitely open for projects to seek green nods. It said the om was without having any rational nexus with public interest, and hence is in breach of environment protection act, 1986.

Article Title: 2 years after death, Supreme Court clears former PM Manmohan Singh in Coalgate case
Article Text:
File photo: Former PM Manmohan Singh

NEW DELHI: More than 11 years after a Delhi court sensationally summoned former PM Manmohan Singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case, the Supreme Court Wednesday gave him a clean chit, closing the case nearly two years after his demise.Special judge Bharat Parashar, presiding over trials in coal block allotment scam cases which were investigated by the CBI under the SC’s monitoring, had on March 11, 2015, issued summons to Singh in the case relating to irregular allocation of Talabira-II coal block in Odisha to Kumar Mangalam Birla-owned Hindalco. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.Parashar, now the secretary general of SC, had declined to close the cases despite the CBI filing two successive reports — on Aug 27, 2014, and Oct 21, 2014 — recommending the same.Since the Supreme Court had barred Delhi HC from entertaining appeals against interim orders of the special judge, Singh moved SC challenging trial court’s order.A bench of Justices V Gopala Gowda and C Nagappan had on April 1, 2015, stayed the summoning order, saving the ex-PM the embarrassment of appearing as an accused in the Patiala House Court complex.On Wednesday, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, who had earlier successfully argued in SC for staying the proceedings against Singh, told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalaya Bagchi and V Mohana that though the proceedings would abate due to Singh’s demise in Nov 2024, the court should remove the trial court’s observations against the ex-PM in the summoning order.Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi joined Sibal to reiterate the request.Both the special public prosecutor and senior advocate R S Cheema and additional solicitor general S V Raju had recused themselves, leaving the court with the task of perusing the CBI closure reports on its own before passing the order.The CJI-led bench said the demise of an accused would ordinarily result in the abatement of case against him. After perusing the closure reports, it allowed Singh’s appeal and quashed the trial court’s order taking cognisance of the crime and issuing summons to Singh.
Article Summary: A delhi court sensationally summoned former pm manmohan singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case. A bench of justices v gopala gowda and c nagappan had on april 1, 2015, stayed the summoning order. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.

Article Title: Supreme Court curbs powers of SC panel, says it can’t pass adjudicatory orders
Article Text:
Supreme Court order may hit similar other statutory bodies

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Limiting the power of National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), Supreme Court has held that it is a recommendatory and advisory body and does not have the authority to pass an adjudicatory order.Abench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih said the commission can send its recommendations to a state or Centre in discharge of its functions. However, an order passed by NCSC is not binding in servicerelated matters, it clarified.“The powers entrusted to NCSC are limited in nature. Clearly, NCSC and its other compatriots under articles 338A and 338B are constitutional bodies with a socially beneficent purpose but quite apparently, the legislature has prescribed a role that is recommendatory and advisory, but certainly not adjudicatory. They are not meant to be bodies taking over adjudicatory functions,” the bench said.The court’s order could be applicable to other statutory and constitutional bodies set up for the benefit of different groups of people like women, the minorities and backward classes.Explaining the clause which says that the commission is empowered to “inquire into specific complaints with respect to the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the Scheduled Castes”, the bench said, “it is therefore clear that while it has powers to requisition documents and receive evidence, it does not have the power to make an order in furtherance of that evidence.In other words, NCSC can record a factual finding and then ask the govt concerned, either the Centre or the State, to act thereupon.”It rejected NCSC’s plea that the word “safeguards” mentioned in the provision pertains to enforcement. “Such a submission is difficult to accept in view of the explicit language of the Article. It certainly does not confer adjudicatory power; at best recommendatory in nature,” the court said.Thus, the commission cannot take up the role of a court or an adjudicatory tribunal and determine the rights of parties, court added.
Article Summary: Supreme court order may hit similar other statutory bodies. National commission for scheduled castes can send its recommendations to a state or centre. However, an order passed by ncsc is not binding in servicerelated matters. The order could be applicable to other statutory and constitutional bodies set up for the benefit of different groups of people.

Article Title: Ahmedabad tragedy: Supreme Court accepts pilot dad's plea not to make Air India crash report public
Article Text:
SG Mehta said the government will submit the final report, as soon as it is finalised, to the SC in a sealed cover

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday accepted the request of the father of the pilot, who died in the Ahmedabad air crash last June, for not making public the final inquiry report, expected in Oct, and the Centre said that it will furnish the report in a sealed cover to the court.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that govt respects the sentiments of the pilot's father and will submit the final report, as soon as it is finalised, to Supreme Court in a sealed cover. The SG, however, brushed aside objections to the ongoing inquiry into the crash of Air India's London flight that killed 260, all but one passenger and many on ground.Appearing for the NGO, advocate Prashant Bhushan attempted to punch holes in the inquiry, terming it to be biased because of absence of independent members in the probe team and said it did not follow the standard operating procedure for such inquiries. The solicitor general said the inquiry is being conducted following prescribed process scrupulously.Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) on July 14 had responded to the petition filed by the deceased pilot's father Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, and said, "In view of the nature, scale and complexity of the present accident, the AAIB has carefully assessed the timeline for completion of the investigation.In all probability, the investigation activities, subject to resolution of the pending external dependencies, are anticipated to be completed within six weeks. ""Thereafter, the draft final report, following completion of the analysis phase, is expected to be ready approximately in Oct 2026," it had said. "As per the treaty mandate, upon preparation of draft final report, the same has to be mandatorily shared with the Accredited Representatives of the State of Design and Manufacture, for comments, as required under the relevant rules of International Civil Aviation Organisation , which in the present case - the National Transportation Safety Board, USA. "
Article Summary: Court accepts request of father of pilot who died in ahmedabad air crash. Centre said that it will furnish the report in a sealed cover to the court. Air india's london flight that killed 260, all but one passenger and many on ground. Air accident investigation bureau (aaib) on july 14 had responded to the petition.

Article Title: 'Uninformed, unacceptable': CJP claims SC order contradicts govt assurance; warns of protest
Article Text:
CJP gives it's statement to the government

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the government honor the July 25 agreement with the CJP? Yes, it must be upheld No, it can change agreements Undecided 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) has threatened to restart its nationwide agitation if the government fails to withdraw FIRs against student protesters, saying a Supreme Court interim order on the batch of PILs related to the protest "rings alarm bells across the country. "In an urgent statement posted on X, CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said Direction No. 4 of the order is a "direct contradiction" to the government's solemn assurance of July 25 that FIRs would be withdrawn and protesters would not be targeted. The Direction permits governments to proceed with existing FIRs and carry out investigations."It was on the strength of that solemn assurance, and in complete good faith, that the Cockroach Janta Party called off its nationwide protest," Das said.The CJP spokesperson expressed apprehension that the government and BJP-ruled states may "weaponise" the order passed by the bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to continue FIRs against individual protesters and subject them to harassment. "This was precisely our concern from day one: that courts could be used, directly or indirectly, to achieve political ends by targeting peaceful dissent," he said.Das also pointed to the fact that the interim order was not opposed by the government's lawyers, despite the Centre being fully aware that talks with the CJP had continued until late Monday night and that a "solemn agreement" had already been arrived at on July 25. "The court's uninformed order is therefore wholly unacceptable," he said."A solemn public assurance given to thousands of young students and protesters cannot be diluted, undermined, or rendered meaningless through subsequent legal developments, in a surreptitious manner. It only results in breach of public trust," Das added.He clarified that nothing in the interim order prevents the government or BJP/NDA-ruled states from withdrawing FIRs or deciding not to proceed against peaceful protesters, as done by Bihar and Assam governments. "The power to withdraw or not pursue such cases continues to rest with the executive. The court has not mandated that governments must definitely continue with the FIRs. That would be a deliberate misreading," he said.Das demanded that the government immediately place the terms of the July 25 assurance before the Supreme Court "so that there is complete transparency regarding the commitments already made to the youth of this country.""The youth of India entered into this understanding in good faith. That good faith must not be betrayed. Institutions of constitutional importance must never be politicised and weaponised to not honour the guarantees," he said.The CJP spokesperson said the deadline for the government to honour its guarantees expires on Tuesday. "We once again call upon it to fulfil every commitment it made: withdraw the FIRs, ensure that no protester is subjected to future punitive action, and honour both the letter and the spirit of the assurance that brought an end to the protest."He warned that if the guarantees are not honoured, the CJP will have "no option but to resume its nationwide protest." "A government that breaks its word cannot expect the youth to remain silent. If the guarantees are dishonoured, the streets of India will once again become the voice of its young," Das said.The CJP had called off its 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar on July 25 after the government accepted its key demands, including the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Article Summary: The cockroach janta party ( cjp) has threatened to restart its nationwide agitation if the government fails to withdraw firs against student protesters. The cjp had called off its 36-day agitation at jantar mantar on july 25 after the government accepted its key demands. The deadline for the government to honour guarantees expires on tuesday.

Article Title: Rajya Sabha adjourned as opposition seeks Shah statement on police action
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha was adjourned for the day Tuesday amid repeated opposition protests demanding a statement from Union home minister Amit Shah over police action against demonstrators protesting the NEET-UG paper leak at Jantar Mantar.The House witnessed disruptions from the start of proceedings. It was first adjourned within minutes of assembling at 11am, after opposition MPs rose to raise the issue and demanded that Shah explain the police action against protesters.When RS reconvened at 2pm, deputy chairperson Harivansh attempted to take up govt's legislative business amid continued sloganeering.Union minister Jitan Ram Manjhi introduced Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill amid din. The proposed legislation was listed for introduction in the day's business. "There is a need to improve and modify the Act made in 2006," Manjhi said while introducing the bill.After its introduction, Harivansh sought to proceed to the next item - the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 - which was listed for consideration and passage.However, Rajya Sabha could not take it up for discussion as opposition MPs continued their protest."So you don't want to run the House proceedings?" Harivansh asked the protesting MPs before adjourning the House till Wednesday.
Article Summary: The house witnessed disruptions from the start of proceedings. It was first adjourned within minutes of assembling at 11am. Deputy chairperson harivansh attempted to take up govt's legislative business. The proposed legislation was listed for introduction in the day's business.

Article Title: 'Modiji clocked it': BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate
Article Text:
BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party Lok Sabha member Bansuri Swaraj on Tuesday used a Gen Z term to praise the steps taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi against the paper leak. She said that the PM had "clocked it" with the anti-paper leak Bill, a term used by the younger generation to recognize a fact.Speaking in favour of the Bill during the debate, she said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution"."I am standing in support of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. This is a transformative amendment. Its necessity is not only evident, but it is also the demand of the present time. Bringing this amendment is proof of the sensitivity of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his committed government. Speaker Sir, when a competitive examination is compromised, its impact is not limited to the candidate whose future is put at stake," she added.The government has proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act to ensure time-bound investigations, speedy trials and tougher penalties for paper leaks and organised exam fraud.Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on Sunday the formation of a high-powered task force, headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, to overhaul India's examination system and make it more transparent, reliable and technology-driven.Addressing students through a video message, PM Modi said the Centre had already taken steps to curb exam malpractice by jailing those involved, setting up fast-track courts and proposing stricter legal provisions, but stressed that broader systemic reforms were now needed.He said the task force would recommend measures to strengthen the credibility of public examinations, with the government acting on its report at the earliest. The Nilekani-led panel will study the use of technology and suggest reforms to improve transparency, efficiency and trust in the conduct of public examinations.The move comes in the wake of recent controversies surrounding competitive examinations, including the NEET row, as the Centre seeks to restore confidence in the system.
Article Summary: Bjp mp bansuri swaraj uses gen z-style praise for pm during anti-paper leak bill debate. Pm narendra modi announced formation of high-powered task force to overhaul india's examination system. The move comes in the wake of recent controversies surrounding competitive examinations, including the neet row.

KANPUR: A candidate who was denied admission to BTech in cyber security at IIT Kanpur claimed to have hacked the institute's website seeking a "fair chance", which he managed to get."The site is hacked, and all I need is a fair chance," the candidate said in a message posted on a social media platform. He said all candidates seeking admission to BTech cyber security programme were given an opportunity to participate in a hackathon, but the candidate concerned could not provide sufficient evidence of his hacking abilities during selection process.

LUCKNOW: IIT Bombay alumnus Jagdish Aphale has been appointed Ayodhya Ram temple trust’s first secretary and made a joint signatory to financial transactions as the organisation seeks to infuse accountability into its functioning and ride out the storm triggered by alleged theft of donations to the shrine.“For banking purposes, the joint signatories are me and Aphale. He has been privy to the trust’s internal processes over the past fortnight as part of his integration.His name was proposed at the trust’s July 6 meeting, held soon after it accepted the resignations of former general secretary Champat Rai and member Anil Mishra.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi remarks row: BJP hits back, calls Congress MP's claim 'a pack of lies'

NEW DELHI: BJP on Wednesday sought to turn Rahul Gandhi 's "idiot" jibe on him, saying it objects strongly if he has used the disparaging term for students but welcomes it if he was describing himself."Rahul Gandhi has raised an issue for Congress and INDI alliance. Why do they consider an idiot as their guru," BJP MP Anurag Thakur told reporters.At a press conference, BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra accused the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha of delivering "a pack of lies" in his speech in the Parliament to mislead the country.He said Rahul "lied" by alleging that bullets were fired by protestors and blaming home minister Amit Shah for it. Better late than never."Countering Rahul's series of allegations against Shah, Patra said he does not go on secret foreign trips like him and was very much in Parliament building when the discussion was happening.Mocking him for his claim that he saw Shah trembling and scared, the BJP MP said naxals and terrorists tremble at the thought of the home minister who has worked day and night to root out extremism."It just shows how far removed from reality Rahul Gandhi is. Article Title: Delhi high court refuses HPV shots stay, but seeks Centre's response
Article Text:
File photo: Delhi high court

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Wednesday refused to stay the HPV (human papillomavirus) immunisation campaign but asked the Centre, Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, and Indian Council of Medical Research to file separate replies in four weeks on the "justification for introducing the vaccine".It was hearing a PIL that sought a direction to the authorities to review the decision to include HPV vaccines in "Universal Immunisation Programme and raised concerns over their long-term safety, lack of informed consent and monitoring of adverse events."Half-baked vaccines should not be administered. We are only to ensure that the necessary protocol is followed," said the high court.The PIL also sought direction to authorities to conduct and publish district-wise and state-wise evaluations before further expansion. The high court scheduled the next hearing for October 29.
Article Summary: Delhi high court refused to stay the hpv (human papillomavirus) immunisation campaign. It asked the centre, central drugs standard control organisation, and indian council of medical research to file separate replies in four weeks on the "justification for introducing the vaccine" the high court scheduled the next hearing for october 29.

Article Title: Continue with your duties fearlessly, CRPF chief tells troopers amid pellet gun row
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: As personnel of Rapid Action Force (RAF), a unit of CRPF , face questions for having fired pellet guns at anti-NEET paper leak protesters, CRPF director general G P Singh has come forward to support all his troops taking decisions and actions in bona fide discharge of their duties.Addressing personnel at CRPF investiture ceremony coinciding with its Raising Day Monday, Singh said, "As DG of CRPF, I want to assure each one of you that whether it is an operational battalion or law-and-order unit, whatever decisions you carry out in the bona fide discharge of your duties and which are aligned with interests of the public, the force and the nation, I shall take responsibility for all those decisions and actions. Continue to perform your duties fearlessly. Wherever responsibility or accountability needs to be taken, I will take as the director general".As TOI reported on Wednesday, a CRPF post-event assessment has found that all standard operating procedures (SOPs) and laid down protocols were followed by RAF personnel during the police action against anti-NEET protesters on July 20.In view of this, a source told TOI, no case may be made out against the RAF personnel for causing injuries to 3-5 protesters by firing the metal pellets."Even if a case is registered against the RAF personnel under Section 117 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (voluntarily causing hurt), Section 218 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita will kick in, mandating grant of prosecution sanction with approval to the CRPF DG. At this point, the DG can justify the use of authorised force by RAF personnel, to deny prosecution sanction," said an officer.CRPF probe into July 20 police action, as per sources, has concluded that the force gradient was followed, with pellet guns being used after lower-grade measures like crowd dispersal warnings, tear gas and lathicharge failed to control the unruly elements in the mob.As required by SOP, Delhi police DCP/ACP had, using his delegated authority as executive magistrate, authorised RAF in a signed format, to use civilian force, including firing pellet guns.
Article Summary: Crpf director general g p singh has come forward to support all his troops taking decisions and actions in bona fide discharge of their duties. A crpf post-event assessment has found that all standard operating procedures (sops) and laid down protocols were followed by raf personnel.

Article Title: 'Not going to let him get away': Rahul Gandhi targets Amit Shah over police action on NEET protesters; BJP says 'prove it or apologise'
Article Text:
File photo: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and Union home minister Amit Shah

Rahul ties Shah to police action on protesters

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha on Wednesday plunged into bedlam after leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi blamed home minister Amit Shah for police's alleged excesses against protesters, including firing, riling up treasury benches as Union minister Kiren Rijiju demanded that he either furnish proof or apologise.He also blamed Hindutva organisation RSS for all the ills afflicting the education sector.Government challenged him to prove his allegation or apologise and declared that they would not let Rahul continue with his speech if he did not authenticate or regret making the charge. "You cannot level a charge to grab a headline and get away with it without providing proof," said Rijiju.Union minister Jitendra Singh also stressed that police firings are ordered by a magistrate. He also defended Delhi Police in his reply, saying it exercised "utmost restraint" in handling protesters' march on July 20, a first such assertion from a senior govt functionary."It was made sure that any casualty does not happen," Singh said, refuting the allegations of Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi and other opposition MPs that brutal force was used against protesters.Rahul Gandhi demanded Amit Shah be sacked as home minister and a Supreme Court-monitored probe be ordered into use of "lethal force" against young protesters - raising the stakes in the battle of wits with govt over the police crackdown on students.He said Shah either directly ordered use of pellet guns, shock batons, lathicharge and tear gas on students, which makes him "culpable of brutalisation" of youngsters, or he did not know what police was doing, which makes him "incompetent". "In either case, he has to go," he said, advising PM Narendra Modi to sack the senior minister.Rahul alleged students are still being threatened, with face recognition and Bajrang Dal being used to scare them. "These are our children and govt has no business threatening them or beating them. They have not committed any crime. They should not be punished," he said.He said demand for Shah's sacking was not proforma, raising possibility of the confrontation of last week resuming after the opposition joined parliamentary proceedings to discuss the public exam bill for two days. "Shah is responsible and we are not going to let him get away with it," he said.The renewed aggression from Rahul came at a news conference that he addressed after he could not complete his heavily interrupted speech in Lok Sabha following a clash with BJP benches over his remarks about Shah.After brief adjournments over an "unparliamentary" word, BJP blocked him when he directly linked Shah to the police crackdown. While his remarks were expunged, BJP led by Union minister Kiren Rijiju insisted he tell the source of his claim or apologise.As per Rahul, he was told he would have to apologise if he wanted to complete his speech, but he replied he would never apologise to BJP or RSS.With Shah's photograph on the big screen at Congress's headquarters, Rahul said, "Every child beaten by police should know that this is the man who is responsible for what happened. He takes orders from PM, but he is the man who thrashed you and humiliated you." He slammed Shah for not coming to LS, saying it shows he is "guilty".At the same time, Rahul said he is proud of students who protested and "they had the courage that their parents did not have" to stand up to BJP.Rahul riled BJP by claiming a student told him about three categories of people - "students" who accept they don't know everything; those who think they know everything and pretend to be God, and "andh bhakts" who believe the second category is God.He alleged Dharmendra Pradhan, who had to resign as education minister due to students' stir, was a symbol while the real mess in the education system was created by the RSS.
Article Summary: Opposition leader rahul gandhi blamed home minister amit shah for police's alleged excesses against protesters. He also blamed hindutva organisation rss for all the ills afflicting the education sector. Government challenged him to prove his allegation or apologise and declared that they would not let rahul continue with his speech.

Article Title: Now, just one visit for NEET-UG counselling
Article Text:
JP Nadda reviews preparedness for NEET UG counselling 2026

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a major reform, the Centre has introduced one-time physical reporting for NEET-UG counselling, ending repeated visits to allotted medical colleges for candidates seeking a seat upgrade.Aspirants allotted a seat in the first or second round can now complete subsequent reporting and document verification online while retaining their seat for further rounds.Under the new framework, candidates opting for the “Float” option can complete document verification online and receive provisional admission while retaining their allotted seat for subsequent rounds. If allotted a better seat, the earlier one will automatically be released to another candidateThose choosing the “Freeze” option, or retaining a seat after the third round, must report physically to complete admission formalities, including verification of original documents and payment of fees.The reforms were reviewed by Union health minister J P Nadda on Wednesday ahead of the start of NEETUG counselling.“Earlier, every candidate allotted a seat had to physically report to the college even if they wanted to participate in the next round for a better option,” said Dr B Srinivas, deputy director general (medical education), ministry of health and family welfare.“Now, they can complete document verification online, retain the allotted seat and continue in the counselling process.If they get a better seat, the earlier one will be released to another candidate. If not, they will retain their original seat.”The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) has also introduced online resignation, allowing eligible candidates to surrender their allotted seat through the counselling portal instead of visiting the institute. Another major change is the complete digitisation of admissions under the NRI category.Candidates requiring additional eligibility documents will now upload them through a dedicated portal instead of sending them by email. “Earlier, these documents sometimes landed in spam folders or were missed, delaying verification. The new software allows direct online verification...” Srinivas said.To improve transparency, the counselling system will use pre-populated candidate data from the National Testing Agency, online document verification, NMC-validated seat matrices and enhanced cybersecurity measures developed with the National Informatics Centre.The Centre has also raised the number of assessment centres for persons with benchmark disabilities (PwBD) from 16 to 61 and introduced an Appellate Disability Assessment Board under revised NMC guidelines.Nadda directed officials to ensure a transparent, meritbased counselling process.
Article Summary: Aspirants allotted a seat in the first or second round can now complete subsequent reporting and document verification online while retaining their seat for further rounds. If allotted a better seat, the earlier one will automatically be released to another candidate. The medical counselling committee (mcc) has also introduced online resignation.

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha on Wednesday passed a bill proposing up to three-year jail term and/or fine for anyone preventing or disturbing the rendition of 'Vande Mataram', even as the opposition benches remained empty in view of almost all opposition MPs staging a walkout.The opposition parties - which included Congress, TMC, DMK, RJD Left, Sena UBT - were pressing their demand for home minister Amit Shah to make a statement on police action against NEET paper leak protesters. Angry MPs stood up and raised slogans. At one point of time, TMC MP Derek O'Brien even rushed towards the deputy chairman Harivansh, to make a point of order, but the Parliament security personnel created a barrier and also stood guard in the well.During the debate, Chair called out to opposition MPs who had given notices to speak, but be it DMK's Tiruchi Siva, TMC's Sagarika Ghose or RJD's Manoj Kumar Jha, they tried to steer the discussion to raising the "brutal force" used on students. Even though the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill is a home ministry bill, it was not Amit Shah but Nityanand Rai who piloted it Wednesday.RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha spoke briefly, questioning the criminalisation of insult to the national song, saying that "reverence cannot be legislated".Junior home minister Nityanand Rai, while replying to the debate, criticised Congress for undermining Vande Mataram and linked it to its policy of appeasement. "Opposing the Vande Mataram amounts to boosting the morale of 'Bharat tere tukde honge' gang," Rai added.AAP didn't walk out with the rest of the opposition, and MP Sanjay Singh spoke during the debate. He questioned "RSS's refusal to hoist the tricolour at its office for 52 years".While BJP MPs welcomed the criminalisation of insults to national song, AIADMK MP criticised the practice in Tamil Nadu to play the state anthem after the national song and the anthem.
Article Summary: Rajya sabha passed a bill proposing up to three-year jail term and/or fine for anyone preventing or disturbing the rendition of 'vande mataram' almost all opposition mps staged a walkout, pressing their demand for home minister amit shah to make a statement on police action against neet protesters.

Article Title: Here's why many MBBS graduates can't take foreign licensing exams
Article Text:
The directory lists medical schools recognisedby the local govt or the ministry concerned, globally

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Thousands of students who have completed MBBS are unable to appear for any foreign licensing examination as the colleges they have graduated from have not initiated the process for an "ECFMG sponsor note" in the World Directory of Medical Schools. This is a formal note on a medical college's listing in the world directory indicating that it meets standards set by Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG).The directory aims to list all medical schools which have been recognised by the local govt or ministry concerned, globally. However, colleges listed here might not have sponsor notes that make their students eligible for ECFMG certification, a credential evaluation agency. Colleges can apply electronically for credential verification only after their first batch of graduates, or roughly five years after the first batch is admitted.Usually, colleges start the process when their first batch starts the 12-month compulsory rotating medical internship. However, many students have discovered after MBBS graduation that their colleges have not got ECFMG sponsor notes. Most students who join colleges don't check whether their college has ECFMG sponsor notes till after graduation when they want to sit for USMLE (United States Medical Licensing Examination), UK's PLAB (Professional and Linguistic Assessments Board) or other licensing exams.Many graduates of Kalpana Chawla Medical College in Karnal, Haryana, discovered that their college did not have ECFMG sponsor notes though it admitted its first batch in 2017. Some at AIIMS have not got ECFMG sponsor notes.In response to an RTI query , National Medical Commission (NMC) stated that "as and when any information or documents to update ECFMG sponsor note in respect of Indian medical colleges is asked by ECFMG, the same is provided to ECFMG immediately after due process and approval of competent authority".NMC's response on June 30 stated the submission of information to ECFMG to update sponsor notes on the world directory list was under process in NMC for several colleges.There was no response from NMC and Union health ministry to TOI's queries on whether it was mandated that all Indian medical colleges must apply to ECFMG sponsor notes on time, and on students' complaints on the issue.
Article Summary: Thousands of students unable to appear for foreign licensing exams as colleges have not initiated process for "ecfmg sponsor note" this is a formal note on a medical college's listing in the world directory indicating that it meets standards set by educational commission for foreign medical graduates.

NEW DELHI: A 27-year-old customer visiting a Union Bank branch in southwest Delhi's Jaffarpur Kalan to update his Aadhaar card was killed Tuesday after the security guard's gun went off accidentally.The deceased, Manish Kumar, a farmer, was a resident of Issapur village. He is survived by his elderly parents and five older sisters. Police have arrested the security guard, Vinod Kumar, 53, an ex-serviceman.Police said the incident took place around 10.30am when Vinod was loading cartridges into his 12-bore double-barrel gun.The firearm allegedly discharged accidentally, and the bullet struck Manish in the backVinod later told police that he reported late for duty Tuesday and by the time he started loading the cartridges, customers and bank employees had already started pouring in.The sound of the gunshot sent customers and the staff into panic. People rushed towards the entrance after hearing the loud bang and found Manish lying in a pool of blood.Police received a PCR call around 11.06 am alerting them about the incident.The caller informed cops that the guard’s firearm had gone off and a man had been shot and was critical. By the time police reached the spot, Manish had already been rushed to RTR Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.According to police, Vinod, a resident of Majri village in Haryana’s Jhajjar district, served in the Army before retiring in 2018 and had been working with a private security agency for the past two years.Investigators said he was posted at the bank as part of his security duties. He has two sons — one is pursuing an MD course while the other is studying MBBS.Police have seized the weapon involved in the incident and sent it for forensic examination. A post-mortem examination of the deceased has been conducted to ascertain the exact cause of death. The report is awaited. Cops are also scanning CCTV footage to ascertain the sequence of events.A case has been registered under BNS Section 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder).
Article Summary: Manish kumar, 27, was visiting a union bank branch in southwest delhi's jaffarpur kalan to update his aadhaar card. Police have arrested the security guard, vinod kumar, 53, an ex-serviceman. The firearm allegedly discharged accidentally, and the bullet struck manish in the back.

Article Title: Ahead of dengue vaccine rollout, all 4 strains found in circulation
Article Text:
Dengue vaccine rollout (representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: As India moves towards introducing a dengue vaccine by next year, the country's first nationwide mapping of dengue virus strains has found all four serotypes circulating simultaneously in eight states and UTs, a development researchers say could influence vaccine strategy as infections with multiple strains are associated with more severe disease.The pan-India molecular surveillance study, led by ICMR-National Institute of Virology, Pune, analysed 6,889 lab-confirmed dengue samples collected through 45 virus research and diagnostic laboratories (VRDLs) across 25 states and UTs between 2023 and 2025. It found that dengue serotypes - at least two - were co-circulating in each state and UT included in the surveillance, indicating increasing hyperendemicity of the disease in India.According to the study, all four dengue serotypes (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3 and DENV-4) were detected simultaneously in Andhra, Gujarat, Haryana, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. Fifteen other states and UTs had three serotypes in circulation, while two reported circulation of two serotypes.Researchers found DENV-2 to be the dominant circulating strain, accounting for 51% of infections, followed by DENV-3 (13%), DENV-1 (7%) and DENV-4 (1%).About 7% of patients were infected with two or more dengue serotypes simultaneously.The study found patients with concurrent infections were more likely to develop thrombocytopenia, haemorrhagic manifestations and arthralgia than those infected with a single serotype, suggesting that circulation of multiple strains could increase the burden of severe dengue.The researchers said continuous molecular surveillance is essential to monitor changing dengue virus circulation, improve outbreak prediction and guide vaccine introduction strategies. They noted that several dengue vaccine candidates are in advanced stages of development and that vaccine efficacy varies against different serotypes, making surveillance critical for immunisation policy.The study also highlighted regional differences in virus circulation. While DENV-2 predominated across India, DENV-1 accounted for a relatively larger share of infections in Tamil Nadu (29%), Haryana (38%) and Rajasthan (25%). DENV-3 was more frequently detected in Gujarat (30%), TN(29%), UP (29%) and WB (20%).
Article Summary: India's first nationwide mapping of dengue virus strains has found all four serotypes circulating simultaneously in eight states and uts. The development could influence vaccine strategy as infections with multiple strains are associated with more severe disease.
